what_its_for: Amoxapine is used to treat depression, including depression that comes along with anxiety or agitation. It belongs to a group of medicines called tricyclic antidepressants, which work by balancing certain natural chemicals in your brain to help improve your mood, sleep, appetite, and energy levels.
how_to_take: Take amoxapine exactly as your doctor prescribed. You can take it with or without food. If it upsets your stomach, try taking it with a meal or snack. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Try to take it at the same time each day to help you remember. Do not stop taking this medicine suddenly without talking to your doctor first, as this can cause unpleasant withdrawal effects. Your doctor will slowly lower your dose before you stop completely.
dosing: The usual starting dose for adults is 50 mg taken two or three times a day. Your doctor may slowly increase your dose over several weeks to find the right amount for you. Most people end up taking between 200 mg and 300 mg per day, split into smaller doses throughout the day. Some people may take their full daily dose at bedtime, especially if it makes them drowsy. The maximum dose is 400 mg per day for most people, or up to 600 mg per day for hospitalized patients. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions for your dose.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — unless it is almost time for your next scheduled dose. In that case, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store amoxapine at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep the bottle tightly closed and out of reach of children and pets. Do not use it after the expiration date printed on the label. Ask your pharmacist how to safely dispose of any unused medicine.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking amoxapine, as it can increase drowsiness and dizziness and may worsen side effects. Do not drive, operate heavy machinery, or do anything that requires you to be fully alert until you know how this medicine affects you. Avoid getting up too quickly from a sitting or lying position, as amoxapine can cause dizziness or lightheadedness. Try to avoid prolonged exposure to sunlight or tanning beds, as this medicine can make your skin more sensitive to the sun — use sunscreen and protective clothing when outdoors. Avoid taking other medicines, including over-the-counter drugs, vitamins, or herbal supplements, without first checking with your doctor or pharmacist, especially MAO inhibitors (such as phenelzine or tranylcypromine). Do not take an MAO inhibitor within 14 days of taking amoxapine.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the nearest emergency room if you experience any of the following: thoughts of suicide or harming yourself, new or worsening depression or anxiety, unusual changes in behavior or mood, uncontrolled movements of your face, tongue, or body (such as lip smacking, grimacing, or repetitive movements), muscle stiffness, high fever, confusion, or rapid heartbeat (signs of a rare but serious condition called Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome), chest pain or irregular heartbeat, difficulty urinating, severe constipation, yellowing of the skin or eyes, or seizures. This medicine may increase suicidal thoughts in children, teenagers, and young adults, especially during the first few weeks of treatment. Report any worsening mood or unusual behavior to your doctor right away.
when_it_works: Amoxapine may start to improve some symptoms such as sleep, appetite, and energy within the first 1 to 2 weeks of treatment. However, it usually takes 2 to 4 weeks, and sometimes up to 6 to 8 weeks, before you feel the full benefit for your mood and depression. Be patient and keep taking it as prescribed, even if you do not feel better right away. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor first.
special_populations: Older adults: Use with extra caution. Older adults may be more sensitive to side effects such as dizziness, confusion, falls, and heart-related effects. A lower starting dose is often recommended. Children and teenagers: Amoxapine is not approved for use in people under 16 years of age. Closely monitor for any new or worsening mood changes or suicidal thoughts. Pregnancy: Talk to your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. This medicine should only be used during pregnancy if the benefits clearly outweigh the risks. Breastfeeding: Amoxapine can pass into breast milk and may harm a nursing baby. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding. Kidney or liver problems: Use with caution. Your doctor may need to adjust your dose if you have kidney or liver disease. Heart conditions: Use with caution if you have a history of heart disease, as amoxapine can affect heart rhythm. Always tell your doctor about all of your medical conditions and medicines before starting amoxapine.
